hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with constipation, malaise, nausea, and vomiting. Occult blood is positive. Colon cancer is the third most common cancer and third most common cause of cancer mortality in the US. Left colon masses present with obstructive symptoms (constipation, decreased stool caliber); right colon masses present with iron deficiency anemia from occult bleeding. Workup: colonoscopy with biopsy for diagnosis (NOT just flexible sigmoidoscopy — must examine entire colon). CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast for staging (gold standard for metastasis screening). CEA level pre-op for prognosis and recurrence monitoring. Pre-op clearance: ECG, PT/PTT, type and screen, NPO. Treatment: surgical resection (colectomy) by colorectal surgery. If lymph node positive → adjuvant chemotherapy. Follow-up: CEA q3-6mo, CT annually x 5yr, colonoscopy at 1yr then q3yr.

case_summary: Colon adenocarcinoma. Constipation + malaise + positive FOBT. Colonoscopy with biopsy → CT staging → CEA → pre-op labs → NPO → colectomy. Office → surgery. 90% recurrences within 3 years — close follow-up essential.
